punchline: At Bell Labs, the stars weren't the smartest engineers. They were the ones who had friends to call before anything went wrong.
thirty_sec: Daniel Goleman argues that IQ explains at best about a fifth of life success. In a long-term study of Harvard men, the top college test scorers weren't clearly more successful or happier by midlife. At Bell Labs, engineers with similar brainpower split into stars and average performers. The stars had built networks of colleagues in advance, so when they got stuck, help came fast. Goleman says those people skills can be learned.
question: If two people are equally smart, what do you think decides which one ends up thriving?
